project.name: Share artifacts publicly from the terminal
project.user_value: A terminal user hands one link to a reviewer and reads every comment back where they started.
project.hypothesis: If we let a reader publish what they are looking at and read the replies in place then they will ask for review before the work hardens
project.wedge: The publish path is the one broken link; everything downstream of it already works.
project.outcome: A person who installed from the tap publishes a file and hands out a link that opens for anyone.
exit: A tap install publishes to production and returns a working link
A reviewer comments in a browser and the owner reads it back in the terminal

milestones.name: A - Publishing works from the terminal
milestones.description: A terminal user publishes a file and hands out a link that works. It ships when someone who installed from the tap can do that, not when a binary runs from a checkout. Every change lands in the client repo.

integration_proof.proof: One tap install produces the same working link both from the command line and from the reader's publish key

issues.title: A terminal user publishes a file and gets a link
issues.acceptance: A user runs the client against a local file and gets back a link that works for anyone holding it
issues.milestone: A - Publishing works from the terminal

issues.title: Credential minting does not widen permissions outside the publish path
issues.acceptance: Publishing a file whose path holds no state-root ancestor leaves unrelated parent directories untouched
issues.milestone: A - Publishing works from the terminal

questions_for_the_archaeologist: What does the trunk carry today for publishing a local file to a remote destination?
needs_a_ruling: Whether the architectural parent whose children span three milestones stays open as an issue
